parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A particle of mass m and charge −q, where q>0, moves horizontally between two plates. The upper plate is positive, the lower plate negative, and the electric field has magnitude E. The particle’s weight is mg downward. Taking upward as positive, what is the vertical resultant force?

A. mg
B. qE−mg
C. qE+mg
D. qE

answer.text: B. The field points downward, but the negative charge experiences electric force qE upward. Combining it with weight gives the upward component qE−mg.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Ignoring relativistic effects and other forces, which paths can an electron follow in a uniform electric field in a vacuum? I: straight line; II: parabola; III: circle.

A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

answer.text: A. The electric force is constant in magnitude and direction. Initial motion along the field line gives a straight path; an initial perpendicular component gives a parabola. A circle requires the force direction to keep changing.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Two straight wires cross closely without touching, symmetrically about their midpoints. X carries current rightwards and Y carries current upwards, as shown. In which directions do the magnetic forces act on the left and right halves of X?

A. Left half up; right half down
B. Left half down; right half up
C. Both halves up
D. Both halves down

answer.text: B. Y’s field is out of the page on its left and into the page on its right. With X’s current rightwards, its left half is pushed down and its right half up; the equal opposite contributions give zero net force.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
An isolated conducting rod moves rightwards at constant speed through a uniform magnetic field directed out of the page. Charges have redistributed until each free electron has zero vertical resultant force. What are the electric and magnetic force directions on an electron?

A. Electric down; magnetic up
B. Electric up; magnetic down
C. Electric right; magnetic left
D. Electric left; magnetic right

answer.text: A. For a positive charge, v×B points down; an electron has the opposite magnetic force, upward. Charge separation establishes an equal electric force downward.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: An electron enters a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the field at speed v and follows a circle of radius r. Which source graph shows how v varies with r?

answer.text: Official answer A; editorial worked explanation: The magnetic force supplies the centripetal force: |q|vB = mv²/r. Cancelling one factor of v gives v = |q|Br/m. With charge, mass and field fixed, v is directly proportional to r, so the graph is a straight line through the origin.
answer.evidence: Official May 2023 Physics HL Paper 1 TZ1 answer grid checked on PDF page 3; explanation independently calculated from the visible source question.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A proton follows the circular path shown in a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. On the diagram, draw an arrow to show the proton’s velocity at the marked position.

answer.text:
Official markscheme checked; editorial worked explanation:

Draw one arrow vertically downward from the proton. At the left side of the circle the required centripetal force is toward the centre, to the right. For positive charge with B into the page, v × B points right only when v points down.

evidence.detail: May 2024 SL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6711M, PDF page 9, checked against this exact subpart.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A proton moves in a circle perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B. Show that its revolution frequency is f = eB/(2πmₚ).

answer.text:
Official markscheme checked; editorial worked explanation:

Magnetic force supplies the centripetal force: evB = mₚv²/R, so v/R = eB/mₚ. The revolution frequency is f = 1/T = v/(2πR). Substitution gives f = eB/(2πmₚ).

evidence.detail: May 2024 SL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6711M, PDF pages 9, 10, checked against this exact subpart.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A proton follows the dashed circular path in a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. At the position shown, draw an arrow to indicate its velocity.

answer.text: Official markscheme direction: vertically downward. Editorial explanation: The magnetic force must point toward the circle's centre, which is to the right of the proton. For a positive charge with B into the page, v×B points right only when v points downward. The velocity is also tangent to the circular path.
answer.evidence: Official May 2024 Physics HL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6708M checked on PDF page(s) 10; editorial explanation independently recalculated against the source task.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A proton of charge e and mass m_p moves at speed v in a circular path of radius R perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B. Show that its revolution frequency is f=eB/(2πm_p).

answer.text: Official markscheme derivation; editorial worked explanation: The magnetic force supplies the centripetal force: evB=m_pv²/R. Cancelling v gives v/R=eB/m_p. One revolution has period T=2πR/v, so f=1/T=v/(2πR). Substituting v/R gives f=eB/(2πm_p).
answer.evidence: Official May 2024 Physics HL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6708M checked on PDF page(s) 10–11; editorial explanation independently recalculated against the source task.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A proton of mass 1.673×10⁻²⁷ kg and charge +1.602×10⁻¹⁹ C enters a uniform 0.14 T magnetic field at 4.79×10⁵ m s⁻¹ perpendicular to the field. Determine the radius of its circular path. You may use the centripetal-force relation F=mv²/r.

answer.text: The magnetic force supplies the centripetal force: qvB=mv²/r. Thus r=mv/(qB)≈0.0357 m=3.57 cm.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A proton, charge +1.602×10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.673×10⁻²⁷ kg, enters a uniform downward electric field of 466.7 N C⁻¹ horizontally. (a) Find its vertical acceleration using a=F/m. (b) An alpha particle has twice the proton charge and four times its mass and enters at the same horizontal speed. The flight time through the field is unchanged, and vertical deflection is proportional to vertical acceleration. The proton’s downward deflection is 14.4 mm. Find the alpha particle’s deflection and decide whether it reaches a lower plate 15.0 mm below the entry line.

answer.text: (a) a=qE/m≈4.47×10¹⁰ m s⁻² downward, about 4.5×10¹⁰ m s⁻². (b) The alpha particle has half the proton’s charge-to-mass ratio, so its acceleration and deflection are halved. Its deflection is 7.2 mm; this is less than 15.0 mm, so it does not reach the lower plate.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A positively charged alpha particle moves horizontally to the right at 2.0×10⁵ m s⁻¹ through a downward electric field of 466.7 N C⁻¹. Find the magnitude and direction of an additional uniform magnetic field that keeps its path straight with unchanged velocity. Describe the magnetic field relative to the page.

answer.text: The magnetic force must be upward to balance the downward electric force. For a positive charge moving right, this requires a magnetic field into the page. Equating qE=qvB gives B=E/v=466.7/(2.0×10⁵)=2.33×10⁻³ T.

parts.display_text:
A proton moves perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. Interactions with the surrounding material can change its motion, and the observed circular-path radius decreases. Which change would explain the smaller radius, with the other particle properties fixed?

A. Its speed decreases.
B. The magnetic flux density decreases.
C. Its mass increases.
D. Its speed increases.

answer.text: A. At fixed m, q and B, r is proportional to v. A lower speed gives a smaller radius. The other changes increase the radius.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A particle of mass m and positive charge q travels perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B in a circular path of period T. Starting with the magnetic force, derive B = 2πm/(qT).

answer.text: qvB = mv²/r, and v = 2πr/T. Thus B = mv/(qr) = 2πm/(qT).

parts.display_text: Two identical non-relativistic charged particles enter the same uniform magnetic field at right angles. One orbit has twice the radius of the other. Compare their orbital periods and explain your answer.
